claims: October 2025 was a pivotal milestone for solid-state battery technology, with top international journals Nature, Science, and Nature Sustainability publishing groundbreaking research achieving critical leaps in safety and energy density.
Global giants CATL, BYD, and Toyota have clarified their 2027 mass production timelines for solid-state batteries, marking the industry's official entry into the countdown to commercialization.

A study published in Nature by a University of Oxford team revealed for the first time the two-stage growth mechanism of lithium dendrites (initiation and propagation): lithium metal first deposits in tiny pores of the solid electrolyte, and when current density is too high, local plastic extrusion of lithium triggers electrolyte fragmentation followed by wedge-driven propagation along cracks leading to short circuits.

The Oxford/Nature research confirmed that instead of relying on traditional high-pressure packaging (5-10 MPa), simply densifying the sulfide electrolyte to 99% allows it to withstand higher currents while inhibiting dendrite growth, reducing battery pack weight and manufacturing costs.

A superionic conductor material developed by Academician Sun Xueliang's team at Ningbo Dongfang University of Technology, published in Science, produced prototype batteries with an energy density exceeding 550 Wh/kg (nearly double that of mainstream liquid batteries) that maintain 92% capacity retention after 500 cycles in initial tests.

On October 7, 2025, the Huang Xuejie team from the Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), in collaboration with Huazhong University, published pressure-free interface bonding technology in Nature Sustainability.
On September 2, 2025, EVE Energy inaugurated its Solid-State Battery Research Institute's Chengdu Mass Production Base and rolled the 'Longquan No. 2' all-solid-state battery off the production line.
Since 2025, solid-state battery technology has achieved energy density exceeding 500 Wh/kg and is moving towards even higher levels.

Farasis Energy's first-generation sulfide all-solid-state battery, scheduled for delivery in 2025, uses a high-nickel NMC cathode and high-silicon anode, achieving an energy density of up to 400 Wh/kg; its second-generation product (planned 2026) targets 500 Wh/kg with a lithium-rich manganese-based/high-nickel cathode and lithium metal anode; the third-generation (slated 2027) aims for energy density above 500 Wh/kg.

In February 2025, Academician Ouyang Minggao of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and Tsinghua University called for focusing on a sulfide electrolyte route matched with high-nickel NMC cathode and silicon-carbon anode, targeting 400 Wh/kg energy density and a cycle life of over 1000 cycles.
CATL, using a sulfide + halide composite electrolyte system, successfully broke through the 500 Wh/kg energy density barrier.

Ganfeng Lithium Group's third-generation all-solid-state battery has an energy density of 420 Wh/kg, passed a 200°C hot box test, and its sulfide electrolyte has achieved hundred-ton level mass production.

Gotion High-tech's sulfide all-solid-state 'Jinshi Battery' reached an energy density of 360 Wh/kg, passed extreme safety tests at 200°C, plans to start vehicle validation in 2025, and has received certification from Volkswagen's MEB+ platform.
BYD's blade solid-state battery uses a 'Super LFP' system with a volumetric energy density of 600 Wh/L (a 40% increase compared to traditional ones) and a cell-level energy density of 400 Wh/kg.

EVE Energy's 'Longquan No. 2' 10Ah all-solid-state battery has an energy density of up to 300 Wh/kg and a volumetric energy density of 700 Wh/L, targeting humanoid robots, low-altitude aircraft, and AI applications; EVE aims to achieve 400 Wh/kg and 1000 Wh/L for solid-state batteries by 2025.
Gotion High-tech developed an 'in-situ solidification' production process that effectively addresses the high interfacial impedance challenge in solid-state batteries.

claims: A solid-state battery (SSB) uses a solid electrolyte to conduct ions between the electrodes instead of the liquid or gel polymer electrolytes found in conventional batteries.
Theoretically, solid-state batteries offer much higher energy density than typical lithium-ion or lithium polymer batteries.
As of 2026, the solid-state battery market has yet to reach scalability and commercialization.
Solid-state batteries are found in pacemakers and in RFID and wearable devices.
Reported specific energy: thin-film type 300–900 Wh/kg, bulk type 250–500 Wh/kg, laminate type 300–600 Wh/kg.
Cycle durability is reported as 10,000–100,000 cycles.
Operating temperature interval is -50 °C to 125 °C; charge temperature interval -20 °C to 105 °C.
Materials proposed for solid electrolytes include ceramics (oxides, sulfides, phosphates) and solid polymers.
Solid-state batteries can use metallic lithium for the anode and oxides or sulfides for the cathode, enhancing energy density.
Challenges to widespread adoption include energy and power density, durability, material costs, sensitivity, and stability.

QuantumScape Corporation is an American company that researches and develops solid-state rechargeable lithium metal batteries for electric cars; founded 2010 at Stanford University, headquartered San Jose, California, ~850 employees (2023).
Major investors in QuantumScape include Volkswagen Group and Bill Gates.
In 2018, Volkswagen invested $100 million in QuantumScape, becoming the largest shareholder, and they announced a joint production project to prepare for mass production of solid-state batteries.
In June 2020, Volkswagen invested an additional $200 million in QuantumScape.
In 2020 QuantumScape merged with SPAC Kensington Capital Acquisition, receiving $1 billion in financing, and listed on NASDAQ under the symbol QS.
On June 26, 2022, QuantumScape announced the production of a solid-state battery with a range of 650 km and a charge time of 15 minutes.
At the beginning of 2024, Volkswagen and QuantumScape presented a battery prototype with 1000 charging cycles and only 5% capacity loss, and an energy density at least a third higher.
In July 2024, VW PowerCo and QuantumScape announced an agreement for volume production, with an initial goal of 40 gigawatt-hours of batteries per year.

In October 2024, QuantumScape introduced the QSE-5 B-sample prototype cell: 21.6 Wh measured cell energy at C/5 discharge and 25 °C, 844 Wh/L volumetric energy density, and 301 Wh/kg gravimetric energy density.
QuantumScape's CEO is Dr. Siva Sivaram and Chairman is Dennis Segers (a February 2024 Bloomberg-cited change named a chip veteran as CEO).

A semi-solid-state (quasi-solid-state, QSSB) battery is an intermediate technology between conventional lithium-ion batteries with liquid electrolytes and all-solid-state batteries, using a hybrid solid-liquid semi-solid-state electrolyte.
As of 2023, commercially available batteries marketed as 'solid-state' were in fact quasi-solid-state batteries.

The primary goal of semi-solid-state batteries is to improve safety by reducing flammable liquid electrolyte while avoiding all-solid-state challenges such as high interfacial resistance and poor contact between solid electrolyte and electrodes.
Semi-solid-state electrolytes are typically gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs), e.g., PEO-, PVDF-, poly(ionic liquid)-, and single-ion conductor-based matrices.

claims: As of 2026, the solid-state battery market has yet to reach scalability and commercialization.
Challenges to widespread adoption of solid-state batteries include energy and power density, durability, material costs, sensitivity, and stability.

The article's Challenges section enumerates: cost of thin-film, temperature and pressure sensitivity, interfacial resistance, interfacial instability, dendrites, and mechanical failure (cathode and anode).

The LiPON thin-film solid-state electrolyte developed at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in the 1990s had applications limited by the cost associated with deposition of the thin-film electrolyte and the small capacities accessible with the thin-film format.

Solid-state batteries can use metallic lithium for the anode and oxides or sulfides for the cathode to enhance energy density, with the solid electrolyte acting as a separator that allows only lithium ions to pass through.
Proposed solid electrolyte materials include ceramics (oxides, sulfides, phosphates) and solid polymers.

Researchers solved the mystery of how soft lithium dendrites crack the hard ceramic inside solid-state batteries, triggering short circuits — a key obstacle to safer, longer-lasting solid-state batteries (reported July 10, 2026).

Solid-state batteries could be safer and more energy-dense than today's lithium-ion technology, but finding solid materials that allow ions to move remains a challenge; researchers used AI to discover a hidden liquid-like ion-flow signal in solid-state batteries (reported March 7, 2026).
A July 26, 2026 headline frames dendrites as 'the biggest problem with solid-state batteries' that may finally be solved.

supported.claim: A solid-state battery (SSB) uses a solid electrolyte to conduct ions between electrodes instead of the liquid or gel polymer electrolytes used in conventional batteries.
Theoretically, solid-state batteries offer much higher energy density than typical lithium-ion or lithium polymer batteries.
As of 2025-2026, the solid-state battery market has not reached scalability/commercialization; no company has entered true mass production, and only small-format pilot production exists.
Challenges to widespread adoption of solid-state batteries include energy and power density, durability, material costs, sensitivity, stability, interfacial resistance, and dendrites.
Proposed solid electrolyte materials include ceramics (oxides, sulfides, phosphates) and solid polymers.
Solid-state batteries can use metallic lithium for the anode and oxides or sulfides for the cathode to enhance energy density, with the solid electrolyte acting as a separator.
Solid-state batteries are found in pacemakers and in RFID and wearable devices.
Reported specific energy: thin-film type 300-900 Wh/kg, bulk type 250-500 Wh/kg, laminate type 300-600 Wh/kg.
Cycle durability for solid-state batteries is reported as 10,000-100,000 cycles; operating temperature interval is -50 C to 125 C.
The LiPON thin-film solid-state electrolyte was developed at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in the 1990s; its use was limited by deposition cost and the small capacities of the thin-film format.

QuantumScape is an American company researching solid-state rechargeable lithium-metal batteries for electric cars, founded 2010 at Stanford University, headquartered in San Jose, California, with ~850 employees (2023).
Major QuantumScape investors include Volkswagen Group and Bill Gates; Volkswagen invested $100 million in 2018 becoming the largest shareholder and added $200 million in June 2020.
In 2020 QuantumScape merged with SPAC Kensington Capital Acquisition, received about $1 billion in financing, and listed on NASDAQ under the symbol QS.
On June 26, 2022, QuantumScape announced a solid-state battery with a range of 650 km and a charge time of 15 minutes.
In early 2024, Volkswagen and QuantumScape presented a battery prototype with 1000 charging cycles and only 5% capacity loss, with energy density at least a third higher.
In July 2024, VW PowerCo and QuantumScape announced a volume-production agreement with an initial goal of 40 GWh of batteries per year.

In October 2024, QuantumScape introduced the QSE-5 B-sample prototype cell: 21.6 Wh measured cell energy at C/5 discharge and 25 C, 844 Wh/L volumetric energy density, and 301 Wh/kg gravimetric energy density.
QuantumScape's CEO is Dr. Siva Sivaram and Chairman is Dennis Segers.
QuantumScape uses a ceramic solid electrolyte with an anode-free cell architecture; its pilot line started in 2024 and its mass production timeline remains fluid.
A semi-solid-state (quasi-solid-state) battery is an intermediate technology using a hybrid solid-liquid electrolyte between conventional lithium-ion and all-solid-state batteries.
As of 2023, commercially available batteries marketed as 'solid-state' were in fact quasi-solid-state batteries.

The primary goal of semi-solid-state batteries is to improve safety by reducing flammable liquid electrolyte while avoiding all-solid-state challenges such as high interfacial resistance and poor solid/electrode contact.
Semi-solid-state electrolytes are typically gel polymer electrolytes, e.g. PEO-, PVDF-, poly(ionic liquid)-, and single-ion conductor-based matrices.

Toyota holds the most / over 1,000 solid-state battery patents globally and its approach focuses on sulfide-based solid electrolytes, which offer high ionic conductivity but present manufacturing challenges.
Toyota targets 2027 for initial solid-state battery deployment (a limited vehicle launch).
Samsung SDI is developing solid-state batteries, targeting pilot production in the mid-2020s and mass production in the late 2020s / by 2030.
Lithium dendrites are a key obstacle in solid-state batteries, capable of cracking the solid/ceramic electrolyte and triggering short circuits.

To date, solid-state cells have found real commercial use mainly in **pacemakers, RFID tags, and wearable devices** (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid-state_battery).

## 2. The semi-solid stepping stone

An important nuance: as of 2023, batteries marketed as "solid-state" were actually **quasi-solid-state (semi-solid-state)** cells — a hybrid solid-liquid electrolyte intermediate between conventional Li-ion and all-solid-state designs (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-solid-state_battery). Their goal is to improve safety by cutting flammable liquid electrolyte while sidestepping all-solid-state headaches like high interfacial resistance and poor solid/electrode contact (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-solid-state_battery). Typical chemistries use **gel polymer electrolytes** (PEO-, PVDF-, poly(ionic liquid)-, and single-ion conductor-based matrices) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-solid-state_battery).

## 3. Commercialization status

The headline reality: **as of 2025–2026, the SSB market has not reached scalability or true commercialization.** No company has entered mass production; only small-format pilot production exists (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid-state_battery, https://www.paradigmshiftlab.com/2026/05/the-solid-state-commercialization.html).

### QuantumScape
The most visible Western player is **QuantumScape** (founded 2010 at Stanford, HQ in San Jose, ~850 employees in 2023; CEO Dr. Siva Sivaram, Chairman Dennis Segers) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QuantumScape). Major backers include **Volkswagen** ($100M in 2018, $200M in June 2020, becoming largest shareholder) and **Bill Gates** (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QuantumScape, https://futuregreentech.com/articles/solid-state-battery-race). A 2020 SPAC merger with Kensington Capital brought ~$1B in financing and a NASDAQ listing under **QS** (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QuantumScape).

Recent milestones:
- **June 2022:** announced a cell with ~650 km range and 15-minute charge time (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QuantumScape)
- **Early 2024:** VW and QuantumScape showed a prototype achieving **1,000 cycles with only 5% capacity loss** and energy density at least a third higher (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QuantumScape)
- **July 2024:** VW PowerCo and QuantumScape signed a volume-production agreement, initially targeting **40 GWh/year** (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QuantumScape)
- **October 2024:** introduced the **QSE-5 B-sample** — 21.6 Wh measured cell energy (C/5, 25 °C), 844 Wh/L volumetric, 301 Wh/kg gravimetric density (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QuantumScape)

QuantumScape uses a **ceramic solid electrolyte with an anode-free architecture**; its pilot line started in 2024, and its mass-production timeline remains fluid (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QuantumScape, https://www.paradigmshiftlab.com/2026/05/the-solid-state-commercialization.html).

### Toyota
**Toyota** holds the most solid-state patents globally (over 1,000) and pursues **sulfide-based electrolytes** — high ionic conductivity but difficult to manufacture (https://www.paradigmshiftlab.com/2026/05/the-solid-state-commercialization.html, https://futuregreentech.com/articles/solid-state-battery-race). It targets a **limited vehicle launch in 2027** (https://www.paradigmshiftlab.com/2026/05/the-solid-state-commercialization.html, https://www.yilaipower.com/are-solid-state-batteries-finally-here-latest-progress-from-catl-byd-and-toyota.html).

### Samsung SDI
**Samsung SDI** is developing SSBs with pilot production targeted in the **mid-2020s** and mass production in the **late 2020s / by 2030** (https://www.paradigmshiftlab.com/2026/05/the-solid-state-commercialization.html, https://futuregreentech.com/articles/solid-state-battery-race).

## 4. Remaining challenges

The barriers to widespread adoption remain substantial: **energy and power density, durability, material costs, sensitivity, stability, interfacial resistance, and dendrites** (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid-state_battery, https://www.sciencedaily.com/news/matter_energy/batteries/). Of these, **lithium dendrites** are a central obstacle — they can crack the solid/ceramic electrolyte and trigger short circuits (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid-state_battery, https://www.sciencedaily.com/news/matter_energy/batteries/). Sulfide electrolytes (Toyota's bet) add manufacturing difficulty on top of these issues (https://www.paradigmshiftlab.com/2026/05/the-solid-state-commercialization.html).

## 5. Bottom line

Solid-state batteries are **technically progressing but not yet commercialized at scale.** 2024 brought the strongest evidence yet of viability — QuantumScape's QSE-5 B-sample and 1,000-cycle VW prototype, plus a 40 GWh production agreement — yet every major player's mass-production timeline still sits in the **late 2020s to 2030** window. The honest summary is a familiar one: the chemistry works in the lab and in pilot lines, but dendrites, interfacial resistance, sulfide manufacturability, and cost keep true mass production just over the horizon.

> **Evidence caveat:** This report relies on a supplied claim set drawn primarily from Wikipedia and a small number of analyst/industry articles. The commercialization details (patent counts, production targets, prototype specs) are concentrated in two to three secondary sources, so the picture of player-specific progress should be treated as indicative rather than definitive.

> **Evidence caveat:** This report relies on a supplied claim set drawn primarily from Wikipedia and a small number of analyst/industry articles. The commercialization details (patent counts, production targets, prototype specs) are concentrated in two to three secondary sources, so the picture of player-specific progress should be treated as indicative rather than definitive.
